title: Guide, Verify, Solve — Anirban Chatterjee, Sonar

primary.label: Coding Agents & Software Engineering
primary.rationale: The talk's core subject is AI coding agents and their integration into software engineering workflows. Chatterjee presents ACDC (Agent-Centric Development Cycle) for coding, discusses AI tools like Cursor in the IDE/PR loop, and frames verification as wrapping the code generation process. Sonar's products (SonarQube, Gitarr, Sonar Vortex) operate in the code generation, review, and CI/CD pipeline space. The inclusion criteria for coding_agents_software_engineering explicitly covers 'coding agents, software-engineering agents, or AI-in-the-IDE/PR loop' and 'code generation, repair, or review as the main product,' which matches this talk's focus on agent-centric code generation, verification, and remediation.

secondary.label: Evaluation, Testing & Benchmarking
secondary.rationale: Multi-layered verification is the central methodology proposed. The talk covers static analysis, LLM-driven code review, quality gates, and Sonar's LLM leaderboard evaluating models across approximately 4,000 coding tasks using correctness, complexity, maintainability, reliability, and security metrics. Verification methodology and measurement of AI-generated code quality are core themes.

secondary.label: Security, Safety, Identity & Governance
secondary.rationale: Zero-trust principles, shift-left security, same-day CVE exploitation, and compliance audit trails are discussed as key drivers for verification adoption. However, security is a supporting theme within the broader software engineering and verification framework rather than the primary focus on AI system security or governance.

secondary.label: Observability, Reliability & LLMOps
secondary.rationale: Quality gates in CI/CD pipelines, code quality monitoring at scale (750 billion lines daily), and maintaining verification consistency across teams touch on LLMOps and reliability concerns. These are operational aspects of the verification framework rather than the central focus.

domains.label: Coding Assistants
domains.rationale: The talk is fundamentally about AI coding tools (Cursor), IDE agents, PR review agents, code generation agents, and remediation agents in the software development workflow.

domains.label: Developer Platforms
domains.rationale: Sonar provides developer tooling platforms (SonarQube, Gitarr, Sonar Vortex) that engineering teams build on for code quality, verification, and CI/CD integration.

domains.label: Enterprise Operations
domains.rationale: Enterprise compliance, audit trails, team-wide standardization, and bounded autonomy governance are discussed as organizational concerns, though these are secondary to the core coding agent and verification themes.

summary: Anirban Chatterjee (Sonar, Senior Director Product & Solutions Marketing) presents "Guide, Verify, Solve" — Sonar's framework for managing code quality in the era of AI-generated code. He argues that AI coding tools create "verification debt," citing a Carnegie Mellon study (MSR 2026) where AI tools (Cursor) produced a productivity spike lasting ~3 months while static analysis warnings and code complexity persisted. Human review is compromised: a Wharton study found people followed deliberately wrong AI advice ~80% of the time ("cognitive surrender"). He proposes two principles — zero-trust (treat all code as from unknown origin, verify with a different method than generation) and multi-layered (combine computational + LLM-driven review because no single technique catches all issue types across syntax, data flow, architecture, and control flow). These are operationalized through ACDC (Agent-Centric Development Cycle): Guide (context/constraints before generation), Verify (multi-layered quality/security/compliance), Solve (agent-driven remediation). Sonar's products implement ACDC: SonarQube for multi-layered static analysis, Sonar Vortex (GA) for in-loop real-time verification during code generation, Gitar for AI-driven PR review and CI automation, and a Remediation Agent for tech debt backlog. Verification runs in both inner agentic loops (real-time during code writing) and outer CI/CD loops (PR review with quality gates). He recommends bounded autonomy for agents, standardized single-platform verification across teams, and developer orchestration tools. Sonar reports 7M developers and 750B lines analyzed daily.
whyItMatters: The software engineering and AI concepts in this talk form a single causal narrative: AI coding tools create a novel quality problem (verification debt from productivity spike decay and context limitations) that traditional SE practices (human code review, post-hoc static analysis) cannot solve alone, because human reviewers exhibit cognitive surrender and no single verification technique catches all issue types. The solution requires both SE foundations (multi-layered verification, quality gates, shift-left security, static analysis at scale) and AI-specific innovations (ACDC framework, in-loop agent verification, remediation agents, context provisioning). The interplay between bounded autonomy (governance) and standardized verification (engineering practice) represents the organizational dimension of making AI coding safe at scale. Understanding both domains together is essential because AI-generated code creates failure modes that traditional SE practices alone cannot address (rubber-stamping, context deficits, model-specific quality profiles), while AI-specific verification approaches still rely on foundational SE principles (static analysis, CI/CD integration, quality gates). The talk's value lies precisely in this bridge: it connects the empirical evidence of AI code quality problems (CMU and Wharton studies) to a concrete operational framework (ACDC) backed by real products (SonarQube, Sonar Vortex, Gitar, Remediation Agent).
temporalContext: The video was published on 2026-08-09 by the AI Engineer YouTube channel, likely recorded at or around the AI Engineer World's Fair 2026. Sonar Vortex and SonarQube Remediation Agent were announced as GA on 2026-06-30, approximately six weeks before the video publication. The CMU study was published as arXiv preprint 2511.04427 in late 2025 and accepted at MSR 2026. The Wharton study was published via Wharton Executive Education around May 2026. Sonar's 2026 State of Code Developer Survey was released January 2026. Research was conducted as of 2026-08-23. The talk reflects the state of AI coding tool adoption in mid-2026, when AI-generated code had reached 42% of committed enterprise code per Sonar's survey.
takeaways: AI coding tools produce a temporary productivity spike (~3 months) but leave persistent increases in code complexity and static analysis warnings, creating verification debt
Verification debt scales with application criticality: short-lived internal tools can tolerate quality gaps, but large codebases with adversarial users cannot
Human review is unreliable for AI-generated code: people followed deliberately wrong AI advice nearly 80% of the time (Wharton study)
Verification must be zero trust and multi-layered: no single technique catches syntax, data flow, architecture, and control flow issues simultaneously
ACDC framework wraps generation with Guide (constraints/guardrails), Verify (multi-layered quality/security/compliance), and Solve (agent-driven remediation) phases
Verification must run in both inner agentic loops (real-time, during code writing) and outer CI/CD loops (PR review with quality gates)
Organizations should establish bounded autonomy for AI agents and standardize on a single independent multi-layered verification platform across all teams and tools to eliminate blind spots
Different AI models have different quality profiles: Claude Sonnet excels at correctness while Claude Opus is better for maintainability, security, and lower complexity
Sonar Vortex provides in-loop verification so agents fix issues immediately before they propagate; a remediation agent tackles tech debt backlog at scale

concepts.name: Agent-Centric Development Cycle (ACDC)
concepts.explanation: Sonar's framework for AI agent development with three phases: Guide (providing context, guardrails, and constraints before generation), Verify (multi-layered reasoning-based verification across quality, security, and compliance), and Solve (remediating issues by giving agents tools and agency to fix them).
concepts.importance: The central organizing framework of the talk; provides the structural model for how verification wraps AI code generation across both inner agentic loops and outer CI/CD loops.

concepts.name: Productivity Spike Decay
concepts.explanation: AI coding tools produce a temporary productivity increase (~3 months) that returns to baseline while code complexity and quality issues persist. The CMU study found a 281% increase in lines of code in month 1, declining to baseline by month 3.
concepts.importance: The empirical evidence for verification debt; demonstrates that AI coding gains are transient while quality costs are permanent, undermining the case for relying on AI productivity without verification.

concepts.name: Cognitive Surrender / Human Over-Trust in AI
concepts.explanation: A Wharton study found participants followed correct AI advice ~93% of the time but also followed deliberately wrong AI advice ~80% of the time. This 'cognitive surrender' effect means human review is unreliable for auditing AI output.
concepts.importance: Removes human review as a viable safety net for AI-generated code; justifies the need for automated, independent verification rather than relying on developer judgment.

concepts.name: AI Model Quality Profiling
concepts.explanation: Different AI models have different quality profiles across coding dimensions. Sonar's LLM leaderboard evaluates models on ~4,000 coding tasks using correctness, complexity, maintainability, reliability, and security metrics. No model is perfect, so verification is always needed.
concepts.importance: Shows that model selection alone cannot solve the quality problem; different models excel at different dimensions, and all have weaknesses that require verification.

concepts.name: In-Loop Agent Verification
concepts.explanation: Sonar Vortex provides real-time verification inside the agent's coding loop, injecting project context before code generation and verifying every change as it is written. Agents cannot proceed until passing verification grade is achieved.
concepts.importance: The inner-loop technical mechanism of ACDC; prevents issue propagation across iterative agent actions and reduces token waste from rework.

concepts.name: AI Remediation Agent
concepts.explanation: An autonomous AI agent that tackles technical debt backlog at scale by generating fixes, verifying them, and raising ready-to-merge PRs. It operates asynchronously and addresses both backlog issues and issues in latest pull requests.
concepts.importance: The Solve phase of ACDC; makes remediation scalable without manual developer effort, addressing the accumulated debt that verification identifies.

concepts.name: Context Provisioning for AI Agents
concepts.explanation: Providing AI coding agents with project-specific context — architectural constraints, coding standards, dependencies, and quality criteria — before code generation to improve output quality and reduce verification burden.
concepts.importance: The Guide phase of ACDC; proactively reduces verification debt by giving agents the information they need to write better code from the start.

concepts.name: Bounded Autonomy for AI Agents
concepts.explanation: Governance guidelines giving AI agents freedom to generate code while enforcing centralized verification and constraints. Agents operate within defined boundaries with independent verification as a non-negotiable gate.
concepts.importance: Bridges AI agent governance with software engineering practice; defines the policy framework within which ACDC operates.

concepts.name: Token Efficiency Through Verification
concepts.explanation: In-loop verification reduces token consumption by catching issues early, preventing agents from thrashing on poorly generated code. Sonar reports up to 36% token reduction with Sonar Vortex.
concepts.importance: Addresses the economic dimension of AI coding; verification is not just a quality measure but also a cost optimization that makes agentic development more efficient.

concepts.name: Verification Debt
concepts.explanation: The quality gap created by AI-generated code that scales with application criticality. A CMU study showed AI tools produce temporary productivity gains (~3 months) while code complexity and static analysis warnings persist, creating an accumulating debt that must be repaid through verification.
concepts.importance: Central framing concept of the talk; explains why traditional code review and quality practices are insufficient for AI-generated code and motivates the entire ACDC framework.

concepts.name: Zero-Trust Code Verification
concepts.explanation: Treating all code as potentially from any source (human or AI) and verifying it with a different methodology than what generated it. Code origin is unknown and untrusted by default.
concepts.importance: One of two core principles proposed for automated verification; shifts the security model from trust-based review to independent verification regardless of code provenance.

concepts.name: Multi-Layered Verification
concepts.explanation: Using multiple complementary verification techniques (computational/static analysis + LLM-driven review) because no single approach catches all issue types across syntax, data flow, architecture, and control flow dimensions.
concepts.importance: Second core principle; the technical foundation for why SonarQube combines rule-based engines with AI-driven analysis to achieve comprehensive coverage.

concepts.name: Shift-Left Security
concepts.explanation: Moving security verification earlier in the development lifecycle, made critical by same-day CVE exploitation. Security issues must be caught during code generation, not after deployment.
concepts.importance: A key customer driver for adopting verification in agentic workflows; justifies embedding security checks in the inner agentic loop rather than only in CI/CD.

concepts.name: Quality Gates in CI/CD
concepts.explanation: Automated checkpoints in CI/CD pipelines that prevent unverified or failing code from reaching production. Quality gates enforce multi-layered verification on AI-generated pull requests.
concepts.importance: The enforcement mechanism for the outer loop of ACDC; ensures verification is not optional and unverified code cannot be merged.

concepts.name: Technical Debt Backlog Remediation
concepts.explanation: Accumulated code quality issues requiring remediation at scale. The SonarQube Remediation Agent addresses this by autonomously generating, verifying, and raising ready-to-merge PRs for backlog issues.
concepts.importance: The Solve phase of ACDC addresses the backlog that verification debt creates over time, making remediation scalable and automated rather than manual.

concepts.name: Bounded Autonomy for Agents
concepts.explanation: Establishing guidelines that give AI agents freedom to generate code while enforcing centralized verification and constraints. Agents operate within defined boundaries with independent verification.
concepts.importance: A key organizational recommendation; balances agent productivity with safety by defining what agents can do autonomously vs. what requires verification gates.

concepts.name: Standardized Verification Platform
concepts.explanation: Standardizing on a single independent multi-layered verification platform across all projects, teams, developers, and AI coding tools to eliminate blind spots from siloed tools.
concepts.importance: The closing strategic recommendation; addresses the organizational problem of fragmented tooling creating coverage gaps that allow quality issues to slip through.

concepts.name: In-Loop Verification During Code Generation
concepts.explanation: Real-time verification embedded in the agent's coding loop that catches and fixes issues immediately before they propagate to future agentic loops or the CI/CD pipeline.
concepts.importance: The inner-loop component of ACDC; prevents the compounding effect of issues being carried forward across iterative agent actions.

concepts.name: Static Analysis at Scale
concepts.explanation: Automated code quality and security analysis applied across large codebases. SonarQube implements multi-layered static analysis covering syntax, data flow, architectural, and control flow issues across languages, and was used in the CMU study to track static analysis warnings.
concepts.importance: The foundational computational verification layer in ACDC; provides deterministic, repeatable findings that complement LLM-driven review.

sections.title: Introduction and Industry Context
sections.summary: Chatterjee introduces himself as Sonar product marketing, frames AI software development as transitioning from experimentation to engineering, and argues that safety and trust mechanisms are needed to scale AI coding across diverse use cases.

sections.title: Carnegie Mellon Study and Verification Debt
sections.summary: Presents a Carnegie Mellon study of GitHub projects showing AI tools produced a temporary productivity spike lasting about three months, with persistent increases in static analysis warnings and code complexity. Introduces verification debt as the quality gap that scales with application criticality, from low-stakes internal tools to large codebases with adversarial users.

sections.title: Model Diversity and Sonar's LLM Leaderboard
sections.summary: Explains that models are diverse with different quality profiles. Presents Sonar's LLM leaderboard evaluating models on roughly 4,000 coding tasks across correctness, complexity, maintainability, reliability, and security. Shows Claude Sonnet excelling at correctness while Claude Opus is preferable for maintainability, security, and lower complexity.

sections.title: Limitations of Human Review and Wharton Study
sections.summary: Cites a Wharton study where participants followed correct AI advice 92.7% of the time but followed deliberately wrong AI advice nearly 80% of the time. Argues this rubber-stamping effect is surely happening in code review. Distinguishes deterministic, provable code from unpredictable software, making automated verification essential.

sections.title: Zero Trust and Multi-Layered Verification
sections.summary: Defines two core principles for automated verification: zero trust—treating all code as potentially from any source, verified by a different methodology than what wrote it—and multi-layered—using multiple complementary techniques because no single approach catches all issue types across syntax, data flow, architecture, and control flow.

sections.title: ACDC Framework: Guide, Verify, Solve
sections.summary: Introduces ACDC (Agent-Centric Development Cycle) with three phases: Guide (providing guardrails, context, and constraints before generation), Verify (multi-layered, reasoning-based verification across quality, security, and compliance—the most important and fastest-to-implement step), and Solve (remediating issues by giving agents the tools and agency to fix them). Emphasizes that verification must use both computational review and LLM-driven review.

sections.title: Customer Drivers for Verification Adoption
sections.summary: Describes why customers adopt verification across AI coding processes: consistent verification via a standard rulebook across all projects and teams, effective AI tool usage including token efficiency and matching models to projects, shift-left security given CVEs are exploited same-day, and maintaining compliance with audit trails proving verification runs constantly and consistently.

sections.title: SonarQube, Gitarr, and Sonar Vortex
sections.summary: Presents SonarQube as a zero-trust multi-layered verification platform across syntax, data flow, architectural, and control flow issues in any language. Announces the Gitarr acquisition for AI code review and CI workflow automation with configurable auto-fix and auto-merge. Announces Sonar Vortex (GA) for in-loop agent verification and a remediation agent for tackling tech debt backlog at scale.

sections.title: Detailed ACDC Flow and Demo
sections.summary: Breaks down the ACDC flow: pre-loop specs (architectural constraints, coding standards, dependencies, quality criteria); inner loop (context provisioning, code generation, in-loop verification with immediate issue fixing via Sonar Vortex); outer CI/CD loop (PR flow with Gitarr LLM review and SonarQube computational review enforcing quality gates). Demos Sonar Vortex with Cursor showing real-time verification and fixing. Notes Sonar data shows customers achieve higher success from AI coding tools.

sections.title: Key Takeaways and Closing
sections.summary: Closes with four recommendations: establish bounded autonomy guidelines giving AI agents freedom to generate code while enforcing centralized verification and constraints; implement ACDC with context, independent verification metrics, and agent-driven remediation; equip developers with orchestration tools to design context frameworks and processes; and standardize on a single independent multi-layered verification platform across all projects, teams, developers, and AI coding tools to eliminate blind spots from siloed tools. Notes Sonar has over 7 million developers and analyzes close to 750 billion lines of code daily, and is a Gartner Magic Quadrant leader.

organization.name: Sonar
organization.summary: Sonar (formerly SonarSource Sàrl) is a global leader in AI code verification and governance, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland with offices in Austin, Texas. Founded in 2008, Sonar provides the SonarQube platform for automated code quality and security analysis, trusted by 7M+ developers across 75% of the Fortune 100 and analyzing 750B+ lines of code daily. The company rebranded from SonarSource to Sonar in February 2023. In 2026, Sonar introduced Sonar Vortex (in-loop agentic code verification, GA June 30, 2026), the SonarQube Remediation Agent (autonomous tech debt remediation, GA June 30, 2026), and acquired Gitar (AI-native code review) on May 21, 2026. Sonar is a Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for Technical Debt Management. CEO is Tariq Shaukat.

technologies.label: Agent-Centric Development Cycle (ACDC)
technologies.summary: ACDC (Agent-Centric Development Cycle) is Sonar's three-phase protocol for managing AI code generation: Guide (injecting project context, architectural constraints, coding standards, dependencies, and quality criteria before generation), Verify (multi-layered computational and LLM-driven verification across quality, security, and compliance), and Solve (agent-driven remediation of identified issues). It wraps AI code generation with verification in both inner agentic loops (real-time during code writing) and outer CI/CD loops (PR review with quality gates), treating all code as untrusted regardless of origin per the zero-trust principle. The SonarQube CLI exposes all three stages as developer commands with sub-100ms latency per file.
technologies.role: Central organizing framework of the talk; the video title 'Guide, Verify, Solve' directly references ACDC's three phases. Chatterjee presents ACDC as the solution to verification debt, with a detailed flowchart showing inner agentic loops and outer CI/CD loops with verification at both levels.

technologies.label: SonarQube Multi-Layered Static Analysis
technologies.summary: SonarQube is Sonar's multi-layered static analysis platform serving as the independent trust and verification engine in the ACDC framework. It performs computational code review across syntax, data flow, architectural, and control flow dimensions in any programming language, providing deterministic, repeatable findings with low false-positive rates that complement LLM-driven review. SonarQube was used in the CMU study to track the ~30% increase in static analysis warnings and ~42% increase in code complexity from AI coding tool adoption. It powers the Sonar LLM Leaderboard for evaluating model quality profiles and provides the AI Code Assurance quality gate system for AI-generated code.
technologies.role: Core static analysis platform described as zero-trust multi-layered verification across syntax, data flow, architecture, and control flow issues in any language. Also used in the CMU study to measure code quality degradation from AI tools, and powers the LLM Leaderboard demonstrated in the talk.

technologies.label: Sonar Vortex In-Loop Agent Verification
technologies.summary: Sonar Vortex is Sonar's GA product for in-loop agent verification, implementing the Guide and Verify phases of ACDC inside the AI agent's coding loop. It injects project-specific context (architectural constraints, coding standards, dependencies, security information) before code generation and verifies every change in real time using SonarQube's algorithmic analysis with CI-level precision. Agents cannot declare tasks complete until all modified files pass verification, preventing issue propagation across iterative agentic loops. It consolidates the previously separate Sonar Context Augmentation and SonarQube Agentic Analysis products and works with Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, and Antigravity. Sonar reports up to 36% token consumption reduction.
technologies.role: Featured product with live demo showing real-time verification and fixing during code generation with Cursor. The demo showed the agent retrieving context, writing code, calling verification, fixing flagged issues, and not proceeding until a passing grade was achieved.

technologies.label: AI-Driven Code Review and Remediation Agents
technologies.summary: This family encompasses Sonar's autonomous AI agents for code review and remediation that implement the Solve phase of ACDC and the outer-loop verification. The SonarQube Remediation Agent autonomously fixes reliability, security, and maintainability issues at scale, running independent analysis to generate verified ready-to-merge PRs for both backlog issues and issues in latest pull requests. Gitar provides AI-native code review and CI workflow automation with configurable auto-fix and auto-merge in the outer CI/CD loop. Together they automate the remediation of issues identified by SonarQube verification, addressing technical debt backlog without manual developer effort. The Remediation Agent graduated from beta to GA on June 30, 2026.
technologies.role: Both products announced during the talk: the SonarQube Remediation Agent as GA for tech debt backlog burndown at scale, and Gitar as a recent acquisition for AI-driven code review and CI workflow automation with configurable auto-fix and auto-merge.

resources.title: The Agent Centric Development Cycle with the SonarQube CLI | Sonar
resources.why: AC/DC stages: Guide (sonar context), Verify (PostToolUse hooks plus sonar analyze agentic with --depth DEEP for cross-file analysis), and Solve (sonar remediate). The PostToolUse hook fires after every edit and sends file content to SonarQube Cloud's Agentic Analysis API.

resources.title: Claude Code hooks and how Sonar Vortex verifies AI code inside the loop | Sonar
resources.why: Sonar Vortex provides context before the agent writes and verification as it writes, integrating with Claude Code via PostToolUse hooks for real-time code quality feedback.

resources.title: Auto-Detect and Review AI-Generated Code from GitHub Copilot | Sonar
resources.why: Anirban Chatterjee holds the title Director, Product and Solutions Marketing at Sonar. SonarQube auto-detects GitHub Copilot usage and runs AI Code Assurance workflow with an AI-optimized quality gate.

resources.title: [Webinar] How to ensure code accountability and trust in the age of generative AI
resources.why: Anirban Chatterjee is Senior Director of Product Marketing at Sonar, focused on code accountability and trust in the age of generative AI, including strategies for LLM approval, tracking, and performance monitoring.

resources.title: The Agent Centric Development Cycle
resources.why: SonarQube serves as the independent trust and code verification engine for the AC/DC cycle with consistent, repeatable findings and low false-positive rate. 96% of developers say they do not fully trust AI-generated code.

resources.title: Secure Native Plugins for AI Coding Agents | Sonar
resources.why: AC/DC is a framework for guiding agents with context and constraints, verifying what they generate in real time, and solving issues before they leave the agentic loop. Sonar Vortex gives AI coding agents project-specific context before they write and verifies what they generate in real time.

evidence.excerpt: there was, in fact, a temporary spike in productivity, um but it lasted about 3 months and then it went back down
evidence.supports: AI productivity gains are temporary, lasting approximately three months

evidence.excerpt: participants did follow the AI advice 92.7% of the time when the AI was correct, they unfortunately also listened to the AI nearly 80% of the time when the AI was wrong
evidence.supports: Human reviewers are unreliable auditors of AI output, following wrong advice nearly 80% of the time

evidence.excerpt: the code could really have come from anywhere
evidence.supports: Zero trust verification assumes code origin is unknown and verification method must differ from generation method

evidence.excerpt: You need to use computational review, you also need to use LLM driven review
evidence.supports: Multi-layered verification requires both computational and LLM-driven methods

evidence.excerpt: catching security issues up front is extremely critical, especially now that we're in a world where CVEs are announced and then immediately exploited
evidence.supports: Shift-left security is critical due to same-day CVE exploitation

evidence.excerpt: providing your agents with tools in the inner loop, in the agentic loop, to not only get constraints and guardrails up front to write better code, but also run verification as it's writing code in real time
evidence.supports: Sonar Vortex enables real-time in-loop verification during code generation

evidence.excerpt: those issues can then be fixed immediately by the agent so they don't propagate into future agentic loops
evidence.supports: In-loop verification prevents issues from propagating to later loops

evidence.excerpt: We have over 7 million developers around the world using us and we analyze close to 750 billion lines of code across our solutions every single day
evidence.supports: Sonar operates at large scale with 7 million developers and 750 billion lines analyzed daily

evidence.excerpt: establish some bounded autonomy guidelines for your AI agents. Give them the freedom to generate code, but also make sure that you're enforcing a centralized scheme of verification and constraints
evidence.supports: Organizations should establish bounded autonomy for AI agents with centralized verification

evidence.excerpt: standardize on a single independent multi-layered verification platform that is used consistently across all projects, across all teams, across all developers, and all AI coding tools
evidence.supports: A single standardized verification platform eliminates blind spots from siloed tools
